skill.description: Use RunComfy Nano Banana 2 Edit for image-to-image edits, batch edits, background changes, and targeted visual changes with preserved subject identity.

skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown guide for using RunComfy Nano Banana 2 Edit through a local CLI. Most static findings are Markdown formatting, placeholder URLs, or transparent security notes; the real risks are intentional external CLI execution and third-party image processing. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration instruction was found.

remediation.suggestion: Keep the RunComfy command fixed, require user confirmation before installation or execution, and avoid shell interpolation for prompts or URLs.
Warn users that prompts and image URLs are sent to RunComfy. Avoid sensitive media, private URLs, and unnecessary web search.
Document token storage clearly, prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in CI, and never print or copy token values into prompts or logs.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Nano Banana on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image edits often drift when prompts are vague or batch settings change. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a clear RunComfy workflow for controlled Nano Banana edits.
actual_capabilities: Routes explicit Nano Banana image edit requests to the RunComfy CLI workflow.
Documents the google/nano-banana-2/edit input schema and supported options.
Shows single-image, batch, and targeted spatial edit command patterns.
Explains prompt structures that preserve identity, pose, framing, and brand details.
Compares Nano Banana Edit with related image editing and text-to-image models.
Documents exit codes, outbound endpoints, token storage, and download behavior.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a RunComfy account or token.
Requires publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs instead of local file paths.
Sends prompts and image URLs to the RunComfy model API.
Long compound edits can drift and may need multiple smaller passes.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Galleries
use_cases.description: Batch edit product photos with consistent framing, backgrounds, resolution, and aspect ratio.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Variants
use_cases.description: Generate controlled background, palette, or layout variants while preserving the main subject.

use_cases.title: Automate Image Edit Requests
use_cases.description: Convert explicit image edit asks into a repeatable RunComfy CLI workflow with known options.
use_cases.target_user: Developer using Claude Code or Codex

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit on this public image URL. Keep the person, clothing, pose, and framing unchanged. Replace only the background with a clean studio wall.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Product Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit these product image URLs as one batch. Keep each product shape and camera angle unchanged. Use a soft gray studio sweep for every image.

prompt_templates.title: Targeted Object Removal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit to remove only the object in the upper right. Keep the table, lighting, shadows, and other objects unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Controlled Variant Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four controlled variants from this source image. Preserve subject identity and framing. Change only the background color and keep the same aspect ratio.

output_examples.input: A user provides one portrait URL and asks for a background swap.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects Nano Banana Edit, preserves the subject, creates a RunComfy edit request, and saves the generated images.

output_examples.input: A marketer provides several product URLs and asks for matching gallery images.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares one batch edit with consistent framing, locked dimensions, and a shared studio background instruction.

output_examples.input: A designer asks to remove one object without changing the rest of the scene.
output_examples.output: The assistant writes a spatially constrained edit request that names the target object and protects the unchanged areas.

best_practices: State what must stay unchanged before describing the edit.
Lock aspect ratio and resolution when editing batches.
Use small edit steps when identity, brand, or composition must remain stable.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not use private or sensitive image URLs without explicit approval.
Do not enable web search unless the task needs external visual grounding.

faq.question: Does this skill require RunComfy?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on the RunComfy CLI and a RunComfy account or token.

faq.question: Can it edit local image files directly?
faq.answer: No. The documented endpoint expects publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs.

faq.question: Does it send data to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and image URLs are sent to the RunComfy model API.

faq.question: How many input images can it handle?
faq.answer: The skill documents support for 1 to 20 input images per call.

faq.question: When should I use another image model?
faq.answer: Use GPT Image 2 edit for stronger multilingual text edits inside images.

faq.question: Is web search enabled by default?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents web search as optional and disabled by default.
